To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) sensing and response specificity of TFs influence the distribution of autogenous and FFL motifs, respectively, and (2) neutral coregulation between TFs with large regulons leads to the assembly of FFLs, bifans, and single input modules.

(i) sensing and response specificity of a TF determine the type and the frequency of regulatory motifs in which it is involved; (ii) the tendency of a large regulon size TF to establish feed forward loops is a consequence of neutral exclusive regulation, and (iii) neutral exclusive regulation also accounts for the presence of single input modules.

1) the distribution of autotranscriptional motifs depends on sensing specificity; 2) the distribution of feed-forward loops depends on response specificity; and 3) the distribution of single input modules is consistent with a neutral model of evolution.

the assembly of transcriptional networks in E. coli, and the relationship between network motifs and sensing and response specificity of their constituents, the transcriptional factors (TFS).
the emergence of network motifs in the E. coli transcriptional network and the relationship between the assembly of motifs and TF sensing and response specificities.
the emergence of transcriptional network architecture.
